top_stories.title: Hackers breach Microsoft 365 tenants via ConnectWise supply-chain attack
top_stories.summary: ConnectWise shut down customer access to its Cloud Backup service after hackers exploited application identities to compromise Microsoft 365 tenants in a supply-chain attack. The breach involved attackers accessing application identities within the ConnectWise Cloud Backup platform (formerly SkyKick Cloud Backup) to gain unauthorized access to customer Microsoft 365 environments.

top_stories.title: China-Linked Hackers Exploited BeyondTrust Zero-Day to Take Over Remote Support Servers
top_stories.summary: A China-linked cyber espionage group tracked as Armory Castle exploited a critical zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-102764, CVSS 9.3) in BeyondTrust Remote Support servers in late August 2026. The flaw involves improper origin validation in an internal messaging component and allowed attackers to take over Remote Support servers, targeting a key PAM and privileged access vendor.

top_stories.title: BeyondTrust patches zero-day exploited in attacks since August
top_stories.summary: BeyondTrust disclosed a critical zero-day vulnerability in its Remote Support (RS) product that has been actively exploited in attacks since late August. The company issued patches and warned customers to apply them immediately to remediate the flaw.

top_stories.title: Hackers Use Compromised ConnectWise Credential to Sign In to 173 Microsoft 365 Tenants
top_stories.summary: Threat actors used a compromised ConnectWise Cloud Backup credential to gain unauthorized access to 173 Microsoft 365 tenant environments. The attack highlights supply chain credential compromise risks, where a single stolen MSP credential enabled lateral access across multiple customer M365 instances.

top_stories.title: CISA Urges Immediate Ivanti Connect Secure Updates as Honeypots Log 105 Exploit Attempts
top_stories.summary: CISA is urging organizations to immediately update Ivanti Connect Secure appliances following active exploitation of CVE-2026-104935, an authentication bypass vulnerability with a CVSS score of 8.6. Honeypot data has recorded 105 exploit attempts targeting this flaw in Ivanti's VPN/access management product.

news.title: Six Vendors Are Shipping Agent Identity Products. The IETF Has Not Finished the Standard.
news.summary: Six vendors are shipping agent identity products despite the IETF's ID-JAG standard remaining an unfinished Internet-Draft (version -04, expiring November 22). The article examines the standardization gap where commercial implementations are outpacing the formal specification process for agent identity.

news.title: The IETF Is Formalizing the Identity Layer Vendors Are Already Shipping
news.summary: The IETF is working to formalize identity standards for autonomous agents, addressing governance gaps as organizations scale agentic deployments. The standardization effort targets the authentication and authorization infrastructure needed to manage an estimated 150,000 agents by 2028, codifying approaches that IAM vendors are already implementing.

news.title: BeyondTrust Remote Support Zero-Day Continues Trend of Exploited Edge Bugs
news.summary: A zero-day vulnerability in BeyondTrust Remote Support was actively exploited, joining a wave of edge device vulnerabilities affecting Ivanti, Cisco, and Palo Alto Networks. BeyondTrust is a PAM vendor whose Remote Support product is used for privileged remote access management.

news.title: Why Active Directory weaknesses stay open for years in teams with one or two admins
news.summary: An interview with intcube CTO David Fuhr describes a 12-week security cohort where 27 municipalities collaborated to harden Windows Server and Active Directory configurations. The program covered SMB signing, LDAP signing, and Kerberos hardening, using lab testing and weekly sessions to help small admin teams implement security changes safely.

news.title: UAT-11985 Uses Fake Event Invites to Target Taiwan Research Affiliates With Google AitM Phishing
news.summary: An APT group tracked as UAT-11985 is conducting spear-phishing campaigns against Taiwan research organization affiliates using adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) techniques to steal Google account credentials and MFA codes. The campaign uses fake event invites to bypass MFA protections by intercepting authentication sessions in real time rather than just capturing passwords.

news.title: Keeper Security and Tenable Integrate to Streamline Cloud Risk Detection, Remediation and Vulnerability Assessment
news.summary: Keeper Security and Tenable have announced a new integration connecting Keeper's identity security platform with Tenable's cloud risk and vulnerability assessment tools. The integration enables remediation of cloud security findings and secures privileged credentials used during vulnerability scanning.

news.title: jumpserver v5.1.0
news.summary: JumpServer has released version 5.1.0 of its open-source Privileged Access Management platform. The platform provides DevOps and IT teams with secure access to SSH, RDP, Kubernetes, Database, and RemoteApp endpoints through a web browser.

news.title: GhostAction Compromises About 1,900 GitHub Accounts, Targets Over 30,000 Repositories
news.summary: A credential-theft campaign called GhostAction compromised approximately 1,900 GitHub accounts and targeted over 30,000 repositories across 3,000 users and organizations. The attack, observed on October 8-9, 2026 and reported by GitGuardian, attempted to extract 3,174 secrets from public repositories' CI pipelines.

news.title: Cybersecurity Stocks Retreat From Record Highs — Citi Raises CRWD, PANW, ZS Targets On Improving Spending Momentum
news.summary: Citi analyst Fatima Boolani raised price targets for several cybersecurity stocks, including Okta, citing AI-driven security spending momentum. The article is primarily a financial/market analysis piece focused on stock performance rather than IAM-specific developments.

news.title: Canonical releases Ubuntu 26.10 Stonking Stingray
news.summary: Canonical released Ubuntu 26.10 Stonking Stingray, an interim release that includes improvements to enterprise identity integration among other features. The release also introduces post-quantum package signing, Rust coreutils, and privacy-conscious speech-to-text capabilities.

news.title: Ivanti ICS Zero-Day Attacks Highlight Vendor Patching Hurdles
news.summary: A high-severity zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-104935) in Ivanti ICS combines authentication bypass and remote code execution, and was only partially discovered and patched in July. The incomplete patch left a window for threat actors to exploit the authentication bypass flaw in active attacks.

news.title: Anthropic 'SneakPeek' Flaw Is a Silent Zero-Click Threat
news.summary: A vulnerability dubbed "SneakPeek" in Anthropic's Claude Code Desktop application allows attackers to silently steal credentials, including SSH private keys, AWS credentials, and OAuth tokens, via the preview pane without any user interaction. The zero-click flaw enables credential theft from developers without requiring them to open or execute any malicious content.

news.title: Microsoft Disrupts 3 Phishing Kits Linked to Over 1 Billion Scam Messages
news.summary: Microsoft, alongside Health-ISAC, JC3, and partners including Cloudflare, Oracle, and Proofpoint, disrupted three phishing kits—CoGUI, Haozi, and Iron Man System—linked to over 1 billion scam messages since January 2026. The operation targeted phishing-as-a-service infrastructure used by threat actors to conduct large-scale credential theft campaigns.

news.title: Employees Built the Agents. Enterprises Just Bought the Supervisors.
news.summary: The article examines a growing divide between employee-built and enterprise-deployed AI agents and how this affects identity governance and access management. Company-deployed agents are managed through identity governance platforms like Okta, while shadow AI agents operate outside official IAM controls.

news.title: The hidden network: Inside the phishing infrastructure ecosystem powering global cybercrime
news.summary: Microsoft uncovered a Chinese-language cybercriminal ecosystem involving phishing kit operators (Storm-2990) and an illicit marketplace (Storm-3119) selling tools and infrastructure for large-scale phishing attacks. The operation targets credential theft at scale, with Microsoft collaborating on disruption efforts against the network.

news.title: Zero-Days Lurk in Microsoft's Overgrown October Patch Tuesday
news.summary: Microsoft's October Patch Tuesday, described as the largest security update ever, contains multiple zero-day vulnerabilities including defense bypasses and unauthenticated remote code execution flaws. The update is relevant to IAM professionals due to the presence of security defense bypasses that could undermine authentication and access control mechanisms.

news.title: No Identity, No Recovery: Cyber Resilience Starts With IAM
news.summary: The article addresses the critical role of identity and access management in cyber resilience strategies, focusing on the growing complexity of enterprise app proliferation and cloud identity providers. It argues that IAM must be reconsidered as a foundational component of organizational recovery and security posture.

news.title: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 1,000 Security Holes
news.summary: Microsoft released a record-breaking patch batch addressing at least 974 security vulnerabilities across Windows and other software. AI is being credited for accelerating vulnerability discovery, though security experts note organizations are struggling to prioritize and deploy the high volume of monthly fixes.

news.title: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses
news.summary: A dark web service is selling digital scans of over 153 million drivers licenses from the US and Canada, apparently sourced from a Louisiana-based identity verification company. The FBI's New Orleans field office has opened an official inquiry into the breach, which affects a widely-used identity verification provider.
